A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DGS-Net research. Their text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching appendix tables across renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection experiments, feature visualizations, component ablations and robustness results, with additional evaluations in Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds linear-probing results and Effort robustness comparisons.

M1.justification: The equations and described gradient-surgery procedure remain unchanged. However, Figure 2 changes the teacher-image classifier's icon from frozen to trainable, while Section 4.4 still specifies training only LoRA and the image and text classification heads. Whether the teacher-head training procedure changed or the diagram is erroneous remains unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training data, UniversalFakeDetect, AIGCDetectBench, AIGIBench and corruption scenarios. The new linear probing uses existing benchmarks; removing individual generator citations does not remove their evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Effort, already present in v2's main benchmarks, is newly included in both JPEG/blur comparisons in Tables 5–6. The new probing comparison evaluates CLIP and CLIP-LoRA controls against DGS-Net. Existing benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 5.5 introduces a protocol that freezes the CLIP, CLIP-LoRA and DGS-Net backbones and retrains identical fresh fully connected heads. Previously reported training settings, preprocessing, metrics and corruption levels are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds a focused linear-probing analysis intended to test representation transferability and geometric preservation. Tables 5–6 extend existing robustness analyses to Effort. The component ablations and Appendix D gradient-selection analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All retained table values match; v3 adds 12 Effort robustness scores and 12 probing entries. The probing results are internally inconsistent: Table 7 gives AIGIBench accuracies of 62.4%, 73.8% and 82.4% for CLIP, CLIP-LoRA and DGS-Net, whereas Section 5.5 gives 71.5%, 52.4% and 76.7%, reversing the control ranking.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations are retained. Equations 10–11 rename the projection variable from delta f to delta g without changing the optimization problem or solution. No new proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of diagnosing catastrophic forgetting, preserving transferable priors through gradient surgery, and achieving a reported average 6.6% improvement across 50 generative models. The new analysis supports an existing claim rather than redefining it.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly interprets probing outcomes as evidence of backbone transferability and attributes a claimed gap from end-to-end evaluation to fresh classifiers overfitting limited training generators. These interpretations conflict with Table 7. Existing limitations concerning DALLE-3, SocialRF and CommunityAI remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3's abstract adds a project/code-access link absent from v2. Existing implementation disclosures, including the backbone, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training duration, alignment weight and patch selection, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work add recent detection and security references, including MIRROR, M2EA and camera-metadata-based detection, while many individual generator-source citations are removed. The methodological taxonomy and positioning against conventional feature distillation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording edits, shortens the generator listing, expands the explanation preceding the alignment loss, and adds Section 5.5 and an acknowledgment. The publication footer changes, but the original narrative and section order are largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 7, inserts Effort rows into Tables 5–6, changes Figure 2's teacher-head status icon and adjusts table spacing and page flow. Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged; appendix Tables 7–9 are retained as Tables 8–10.

improvement.justification: The code-access statement and Effort comparisons offer limited benefits. However, the added preservation analysis contradicts its own table, including reversing the CLIP versus CLIP-LoRA ranking, which weakens its evidential reliability. Figure 2 also introduces an unresolved teacher-head training-status inconsistency. These reporting problems outweigh the modest additions, while the retained benchmark evidence limits the overall decline.
